People then sign in online with the school code, their own learner code or staff ID, and their PIN. Sync is optional and off until a school manager turns it on. t: How offline sync keeps every device in step
d: Several teachers, several computers, no reliable internet. Here is how records from different devices are merged without losing anyone's work.
x: Home / News and tips / Article How offline sync keeps every device in step Explainer | 19 Sep 2026 In many schools, one teacher marks on a phone while another uses the school computer. The records must come together without one device overwriting another. Merging, not replacing When two devices sync, Smart School App compares them record by record. The most recent change to each record wins, and records that exist on only one device are kept. Nothing is deleted just because another device has not seen it yet. Three ways to sync Over the school Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot, with no internet Through a USB drive or folder backup Online through Smart School Cloud, when a connection is available Whichever way is used, run the same app version on every device so merges behave the same everywhere. t: Five tips for faster lesson plans with the REB template
d: Planning takes time. These five habits help teachers prepare clear lesson plans in less time.
x: Home / News and tips / Article Five tips for faster lesson plans with the REB template Teaching tips | 12 Sep 2026 A good lesson plan is short, clear and usable. These tips work with the official REB lesson plan template. Start from the scheme of work. Copy the unit objectives first, then plan the activities that lead to them. Plan backwards. Decide how you will know learners understood, then design the activities. Reuse what works. Save a good plan and adapt it for the next class. Write timings in minutes for each stage so the lesson fits the period. Prepare one extension task for fast learners and one support task for those who need help. Smart School App's lesson plan generator fills the template from the real scheme of work in English, French or Kinyarwanda, so teachers can spend their time on the teaching ideas. t: Getting more from P6 exam practice
d: Past papers help most when learners review their mistakes. A simple routine turns practice into progress.
x: Home / News and tips / Article Getting more from P6 exam practice Teaching tips | 29 Aug 2026 Sitting past papers is useful, but the learning happens in the review. Practise under timed conditions once a week. Review every wrong answer and read the model answer. Note the topic behind each mistake and revisit that topic the next day. Repeat the missed questions after a few days to check the learning stuck. Smart School App marks written answers against an answer key and lists weak topics. Teachers should review and confirm each answer key on the Answer keys screen before relying on marks for grades. Share WhatsApp Email Copy link Want this for your school?
